name: Document Highlight Focus Pan
use_when: A document, article, screenshot, transcript, or paper image contains key text that supports the narration.
The viewer needs to see specific lines without reading the whole source.
A source image should feel editorial and tactile rather than like a raw screenshot.
avoid_when: The highlighted text is not legible at delivery size.
The highlight would hide the wording or imply a meaning not present in the source.
The document contains private, sensitive, or uncleared information that should not be shown.

timeline_pattern.pattern: source_document -> warm_or_match_adjustment -> highlight_bar_behind_text -> wipe_reveal -> compound -> pan_zoom_to_highlight -> second_highlight_or_exit
timeline_pattern.truth_rule: Highlight only text that is actually present and relevant to the claim.
timeline_pattern.blend_rule: Place the highlight visually behind the text using darken/multiply-style blending when possible.
timeline_pattern.focus_rule: Pan or zoom only enough to direct attention; maintain enough context to avoid misleading the quote.

motion.rule: Reveal highlights in reading order and ease camera moves between lines.

keyframe_values.highlight_wipe_duration: Use a wipe long enough to read as a highlight, commonly 8-24 frames for short phrases and longer for full lines.
keyframe_values.focus_zoom: Use modest scale increases that keep surrounding context visible unless the line is the only required detail.
keyframe_values.pan_hold: Hold after the pan/zoom until the highlighted words can be read.
keyframe_values.easing: Use cubic/eased movement for document pans so the motion feels editorial, not mechanical.

sound.rule: Use a soft marker, pencil, camera, or paper cue on important highlights only; speech remains dominant.

captions.rule: Captions should not cover the source wording; suppress or reposition captions during document inspection.

color.rule: Warm or match document color only enough to fit the scene while preserving text contrast and source integrity.

implementation.ffmpeg: Overlay a semi-transparent highlight rectangle behind text, animate width/crop for wipe, and apply crop/scale/pan to the document segment.
implementation.remotion: Create a DocumentHighlight component with documentAsset, highlightRects, revealFrames, focusKeyframes, sourceContext, and privacyReview flags.
implementation.blender: Use document planes, colored highlight strips, and orthographic camera pans for rendered editorial document scenes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use an image layer, text underscore/shape highlight layers, Wipe Right animation, Darken blend, compound clips, transform keyframes, and cubic ease.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics rectangles with Multiply/Darken-like blend or opacity, Linear Wipe, nested sequence, Motion keyframes, and captions moved off the document area.

common_mistakes: Highlighting text too quickly for the viewer to read.
Covering the source words with an opaque highlight.
Zooming so far into a document that context disappears.
Showing private or uncleared document details.
Using a fake highlight that changes the apparent source meaning.
qc: Is the highlighted wording legible at delivery size?
Does the highlight sit behind or around text without hiding it?
Is enough surrounding context visible to avoid misleading the viewer?
Are private, sensitive, or uncleared details removed or approved?
Do captions and graphics avoid the highlighted source text?
